pains.title: Deposits and prepaid surgery fees
pains.problem: Patients pay deposits and balances before surgery, and cancellations create retained deposits and refunds. Until the procedure happens, that money is generally owed to the patient.
pains.how: Lucid sets up a deposits liability and a monthly rollforward tied to your payment system, so reports separate cash on hand from cash owed to patients.

pains.title: Profitable on paper, thin in your bank account
pains.problem: High ticket prices make margins look huge, but clinical labor, anesthesia and coordinators are often left out, and surgery, injectables and spa lines sit in one pile.
pains.how: Lucid tracks revenue and direct cost by service line, surgeon and location, moves clinical labor into delivery cost, and reports margin by line every month.

pains.title: Devices that leave a profitable practice cash poor
pains.problem: A laser or operating room build out can drain cash even when the tax bill shrinks. A deduction lowers tax owed but does not return the cash spent.
pains.how: Lucid reviews the purchase before you sign, models how many cases or treatments it takes to pay back, and adds the payment to your cash forecast.

faq_title: Plastic surgery accounting questions owners ask

faq.q: Why is my plastic surgery practice making money on paper but I am not taking home much?
faq.a: Often the books mix surgery, injectables, retail and staff costs in one pile, so the margin you see is not the margin you keep. Lucid sets up your books by service line, so you see what each line really earns.

faq.q: How do I record CareCredit or patient financing fees in my books?
faq.a: Deposits are a liability until the procedure, and revenue follows your CPA's accounting rules. Record the lender's fee as its own expense, so a payout that arrives smaller than the sale still reconciles. Lucid matches each lender payout to your sales.

faq.q: How do I do the bookkeeping for a med spa that is part of my plastic surgery practice?
faq.a: Track it as its own line, with package and membership revenue recognized as treatments are delivered and injectable and product costs tracked. If the spa is a separate company, Lucid's consolidated reporting shows both.

faq.q: How much salary should I pay myself from my plastic surgery S corporation?
faq.a: The IRS expects a reasonable salary for the work you actually do, so paying yourself very little and taking the rest as distributions can be challenged. Your Lucid CPA looks at your role, market rate and profit, then sets a plan you can defend.

faq.q: How do I know what a new surgical patient really costs me in marketing?
faq.a: Divide each channel's spend by the number of patients who actually completed and paid for surgery, not by the number of leads. Lucid keeps marketing spend split by channel and, with your booking data, reports cost per paid patient.
